audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven level-chart rows contradict the packet, and every one of them also contradicts the page's own whys. whys[0] says 'Gnar controls the opening' while win[0] says Skill; whys[2] says the trade is 'back to even' while win[2] says Gnar; whys[4] calls Mega Gnar the kill threat while win[4] says Skill; whys[5] says 'the lane is even' while win[5] says Gnar; whys[6] says you outscale him while win[6] says Gnar.
audit.why: Packet chart: Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Gnar, Skill, Wukong — and the gnar__wukong mirror was set to exactly that. Win rate 55.24% over 286 games with the lead arriving late fits the prose, not the enums.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; ratings rescaled at rows 0 and 6. The prose needed no change because it was already right.

audit.why: Gnar's spikes are rage-bar transformations rather than levels: Mega Wallop (flat 7s stun), Boomerang/Boulder 16s at rank 1 reduced when he picks it up, Hop 22s at rank 1, and GNAR! at 90/60/30s. Wukong's are levels 2-3, Black Cleaver, and the two-item teamfight window.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] reworded to hang the level-6 window on Wallop's 7s rather than an unquantified 'respect Mega'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats GNAR! as the tracked cooldown for the whole lane ('Engage only on GNAR!'s cooldown'), but the ability that actually decides a Mega brawl is Wallop, his W stun, at a flat 7s. GNAR! is a 90/60/30s ultimate he may not have at all; Wallop is up in every single trade.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'Mega Gnar ... can rear up on his hind legs and smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies in an area', cd 7 flat. The kit flags it hardCC. Hop/Crunch (E) at 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s is his only escape and the real punish window in Mini form.
audit.corrected: Wallop's 7s stun is the button to bait with the clone; Hop at 22s at rank 1 is the window to commit into Mini Gnar.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears anywhere on the page, so 'when it is down' is untimed advice.
audit.why: Hop 22s at rank 1 and Wallop 7s are the two numbers that make the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Both written into the Don'ts and the ability-interactions box.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] asserts 'your R Cyclone knocks up but you can't buffer his wall-stun'. The brief carries no Wukong kit data and nothing establishes that buffering claim.
audit.why: The kits cannot answer buffering; asserting it either way would be speculation.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the verifiable Wallop timing instead of the buffering claim.

edits.before: Mega Gnar arrives with GNAR! (R) and becomes a genuine kill threat into a wall; your R Cyclone knocks up but you can't buffer his wall-stun, so respect his rage bar and don't stand near terrain when he's yellow.
edits.after: Mega Gnar arrives with GNAR! (R) and becomes a genuine kill threat into a wall; his Wallop stun is up every 7s, so bait it with the clone before you commit. Respect the rage bar and never brawl near terrain when he's yellow.

edits.before: Track Gnar's GNAR! (Mega Stun): His Mega all-in. Burst mini form. When it is down — E-Q + R him.
edits.after: Mega's real threat is Wallop's stun, up every 7s — bait it with the clone, then E-Q while Hop is down.

edits.before: That is Gnar's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Mini Gnar's Hop bounces off you and the wave — 22s at rank 1, punish that.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Mega Wallop stuns every 7s and his Hop escape is 22s at rank 1.

notes: The prose on this page was already correct and the enums were wrong — five of seven chart rows contradicted the whys sitting directly beside them. Flipped rows 0/2/4/5/6 to the packet chart in matched pairs, which is also what the gnar__wukong mirror carries. Mechanically the page tracks the wrong ability: GNAR! (90/60/30s) is named as the cooldown to play around when the button that decides every Mega trade is Wallop at a flat 7s, with Hop's 22s at rank 1 as the commit window against Mini. I also removed an unsupported 'you can't buffer his wall-stun' claim — the brief has no Wukong kit data, so that was unverifiable either way.
